solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First of fixtures, very small with no top and awkward to use

indicators.note: the first letter of the word fixtures is all that is taken here

parts.note: first letter of fixtures

indicators.note: in a down-to-earth sense the top of a word is its opening letter, which is dropped

parts.note: diddly is informal for tiny or very small

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a set of very small fittings with no top that are hard to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: Diddly, as in diddly-squat, is informal for tiny; 'no top' beheads it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fiddly is intricate and finicky, hence awkward or tricky to handle.

clue.text: Pale pants found in appropriate place that's shabby

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are located inside the word for appropriate

parts.note: fit means appropriate or suitable

indicators.note: pants is used as a verb meaning gasps, but in British slang pants also means rubbish, so the letters are messed about

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pale figure gasps on arriving at a suitably run-down spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like a verb for gasping but signals the jumble. In British slang a fleapit is a run-down cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleapit is a shabby cinema or theatre, imagined as infested with fleas.

clue.text: Quickly scribbled and hastily left?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a note ... is written in a hurry
second meaning: to have ... is to have rushed away

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrasal verb covers writing something in haste and departing in haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means rush, so the phrase covers both hurried writing and a hurried departure.

clue.text: Record man serving by a gallery in the open

parts.note: a log is a written record
a GI is an American soldier, a serving man

explanation.surface: A soldier logs his service beside an outdoor gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an arcade or gallery open on one side to the air, common in Italian buildings.

clue.text: This boy is excited to receive book, one for a pastime?

indicators.note: one set of letters takes in, or receives, another piece in its middle
excited letters are stirred up, so the words this boy are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lad gets thrilled at being given a book, perhaps because he loves a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is excited' scrambles THISBOY, and 'to receive' puts B for book inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist is a person devoted to a leisure pursuit, so one who goes in for a pastime.

clue.text: Element of apoplexy noticed after turning over precious stone

indicators.note: turned over means the hidden run is read back to front
an element is just a part, so a run of letters is taken from inside apoplexy noticed

explanation.surface: A fit of apoplexy is spotted after someone flips a valuable gem.
explanation.walkthrough: The run XYNO sits across apoplexy noticed; 'after turning over' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Sibling and children with Yorkshire banker in pamphlet

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a sibling
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, and a river is a banker because it has banks

explanation.surface: A family with a bank manager from Yorkshire featured in a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is the crossword joke for a river, something with banks; the Ure flows through North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochure is a small booklet of information or advertising, much like a pamphlet.

clue.text: Perfect introduction for a trade negotiator?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I DEAL and it is how a dealer might introduce their line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means exactly as wanted, perfect in every respect.

clue.text: Start of this struggle to get rid of Western framework

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from this
getting rid of means discarding, so the western letter is dropped from struggle

parts.note: to wrestle is to struggle

explanation.surface: The first step in a fight to scrap a Western set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' is not a film genre here but just the single letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a supporting frame of a beam on legs, used in pairs to hold up a table top.

clue.text: Standard pair of bridge players with Leo?

parts.note: E and N are East and North, two of the four seats at a bridge table
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A card-table pair and a lion-hearted friend seem to be teaming up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit at North, South, East and West, so any two compass letters can be a pair of them; 'Standard' is a flag, not a norm.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and a standard is another word for a flag carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Pigment exposed to view in French school (not English)

indicators.note: the word for exposed to view is placed in the French school's name
not here means without, so one letter for English is left out of the school's name

parts.note: a lycée is a French secondary school
open means exposed to view, uncovered

explanation.surface: Some colouring is put on show at a school in France, but not to English pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: A lycée is a French secondary school; only one of its two Es goes, and the parenthesis is the instruction, not an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycopene is the red carotenoid colouring found in tomatoes, a natural pigment.

clue.text: Release time in Washington DC among many at work

indicators.note: among puts the time abbreviation in the middle of the rearranged letters
letters at work are busy being rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
EST, Eastern Standard Time, is the time zone of Washington DC

explanation.surface: A prisoner freed in the US capital at a busy time for many workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington DC is on Eastern Standard Time, abbreviated EST.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon, a release from punishment granted to many offenders.

clue.text: Instalments to cover?

parts.note: regular payments made to an insurer in return for insurance cover

explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' looks like a verb meaning pay for, but it is the noun: insurance cover, paid for in regular instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Premiums are the periodic sums paid to keep an insurance policy in force.

clue.text: Check a rental property, Alpine residence

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: Inspecting a holiday rental, which turns out to be a house in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a let is a rented property, such as a holiday let.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is the wooden house typical of Swiss and other mountain villages.

clue.text: One looking hard to seal the end of Conservatism?

definitions.text: One looking hard to seal the end of Conservatism?

parts.words: One looking hard to seal the end of Conservatism?
parts.note: a person with a severer face, perhaps a hardline Tory set on finishing the movement off

explanation.walkthrough: No wordplay is evident; the clue pictures someone wearing an especially severe expression, as if determined to finish off a political creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner is the comparative of stern, meaning harsher or more severe in look or manner.

clue.text: Withdraw money for power drill, say

indicators.note: to draw back is to pull in the opposite direction, so the word for money is read backwards

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Taking cash out of the bank to buy a power drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' reads like a bank transaction but asks for LOOT drawn backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A power drill is one example of a tool, an implement used for work.

clue.text: Artist in best role for representing characteristic of some heirlooms?

indicators.note: the artist's letters are set in the middle of the rearranged words
representing suggests the letters of best role are recast in a new form

parts.note: anagram fodder
RA is a Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: An actor turned artist gets the best part, playing a family treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for representing' rearranges BESTROLE, and RA goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Old family pieces are often damaged but able to be repaired, so being restorable is a quality many have.

clue.text: Secure order in part of hospital? It's not worth considering

parts.note: to bag something is to secure it

indicators.note: the word for order is placed inside the hospital department

parts.note: A&E is the Accident and Emergency department of a British hospital
to tell someone to do something is to order them

explanation.surface: Insisting on a ward order is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a trifle, something too unimportant to be worth thinking about.

clue.text: Diplomatic representative negligent having ignored queen on a railway

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so the queen's letter is dropped

parts.note: remiss means negligent
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A careless envoy ignored the queen while travelling by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: R for queen comes from Regina, as in royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, such as a diplomatic envoy.

clue.text: In short, skilful scholar eclipsing a Conservative of a scurrilous nature

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover over, so the first group of letters is wrapped around the a
in short means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: deft means skilful
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A clever academic outshining a Tory politician, perhaps with nasty gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' trims DEFT to DEF; DEF plus MA 'eclipsing' A gives DEFAMA, then add TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamatory remarks damage a reputation, just as scurrilous ones are abusive and slanderous.

clue.text: Aloof and surprisingly staid group of conservationists

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of staid turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: anagram fodder
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A conservation body is unexpectedly stuffy and standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges STAID as DISTA, then NT is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant describes a cool, reserved manner, just as aloof means unfriendly and detached.

clue.text: Very impatient Chicago gangster? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the phrase Chicago gangster is used, the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Is a Chicago mobster restless? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, so keen or impatient to hear or see something.

clue.text: Bitterness over one at sea in old vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: gall means bitterness or resentment

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of one are muddled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Resentment felt by one sailor aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ONE as EON, placed below GALL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the 15th to 17th centuries, an old vessel.

clue.text: Greek character entertained by support for geeky type

indicators.note: a host entertains a guest inside, so the Greek letter goes within the word for support

parts.note: a tee is a peg that supports a golf ball
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek guest is hosted by a supporter of a nerdy sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A techie is an informal word for a technology enthusiast or expert, a nerdy sort.

clue.text: Special society in time given backing? It's in short supply

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
to back is to move in reverse, so the word for time is turned round

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A special club once given support is now running low on funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given backing' looks like sponsorship but asks for the word for time to be turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty, so whatever is sparse is in short supply.

clue.text: Grant left amid a difficult period?

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the letter for left goes inside

parts.note: a low is a bad time, a low point

explanation.surface: A grant is handed out during a tough spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to permit it, a synonym of allow.

clue.text: Support exercise mistakenly slated

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the letters of slated have been set out wrongly

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A workout is wrongly criticised, though really it gives backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base on which a statue or column stands, so a support.

clue.text: Lodge in Cornish town overlooking person's home

indicators.note: to overlook is to miss out, so the home is left off the town's name

parts.note: Padstow is a fishing town on the north coast of Cornwall
a pad is slang for someone's home

explanation.surface: Staying in a Cornish town overlooking someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' suggests a view, but means missing out: PAD is dropped from PADSTOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge something is to put it away somewhere, which is what stowing it means.

clue.text: A line, sadly paltry, describing several parliamentary groups?

indicators.note: sadly here means poorly or in a sorry state, so the letters of paltry are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A feeble policy line backed by MPs from several parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges PALTRY into PARTY after A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-party committee or group contains members drawn from every political party in parliament.

clue.text: Put aside Victorian novel introducing romance, nothing less

parts.note: She is an 1887 novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: less means minus, so the zero letter is taken away from the word for romance

parts.note: love means romance
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a Victorian novel once love interest is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: She, by H. Rider Haggard, is a crossword favourite for a Victorian novel; 'introducing' simply sets it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone it, setting it aside for later as if on a shelf.

clue.text: Member of parliament with an orangey look?

definitions.text: Member of parliament with an orangey look?

parts.words: Member of parliament with an orangey look?
parts.note: a parliament is the collective noun for owls, and tawny means orange-brown

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sun-tanned MP, but a parliament here is a group of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawny owl is a common British owl with orange-brown plumage, one bird of an owl parliament.

clue.text: Humble writer captivated by academic figure

indicators.note: being captivated means being held captive, so the writer sits inside the academic

parts.note: a dean is a senior university official
me is the writer of the clue, referring to themself

explanation.surface: A modest author is charmed by a college head.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, a sense of humble as a verb meaning to humiliate.
